entities.name: Mariinsky Theatre
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The Mariinsky Theatre in St. Petersburg, Russia is one of the world's great opera and ballet companies, founded in 1783 and named for Empress Maria Alexandrovna. The Mariinsky Ballet Company is arguably the greatest ballet institution in history: birthplace of the classical ballet canon, home of Petipa's Sleeping Beauty and Swan Lake, training ground for Pavlova, Nijinsky, Nureyev, Baryshnikov, and generations of the world's finest dancers.

The current Mariinsky Theatre building opened in 1860, replacing earlier theaters. The Imperial Ballet and Imperial Opera Companies performed under successive directors, but the era of choreographer Marius Petipa (1862-1903) created the classical ballet canon: The Sleeping Beauty (1890, Tchaikovsky), The Nutcracker (1892), Swan Lake revival (1895), and Raymonda (1898) — works still performed at every major ballet company worldwide. Petipa's Mariinsky created the 'Russian style' of classical ballet that became the global standard.

The 20th century brought revolution and flight: Anna Pavlova left Russia in 1907, Rudolf Nureyev defected to the West in 1961 (Paris), Mikhail Baryshnikov defected in 1974 (Canada). Each defection brought Russian ballet technique to Western companies. Valery Gergiev, conductor from 1988 and artistic director from 1996, transformed the Mariinsky into a year-round festival theater with new venues including the Mariinsky II (2013) and concert hall. Gergiev's pro-Putin stance cost him the Munich Philharmonic directorship in 2022.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Mariinsky Theatre created classical ballet as a global art form through the Petipa-Tchaikovsky collaboration, and its training of Pavlova, Nijinsky, Nureyev, and Baryshnikov shaped the 20th century's entire dance culture.
